Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 15, "heading": "CHAPTER 13. THE SEQUEL OF MY RESOLUTION", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u015-b0062", "target": "Сначала я расспрашивал о моей тётушке лодочников и получил разные ответы. Один сказал, что она живёт на маяке Саут-Форленд и опалила там себе бакенбарды; другой — что она пришвартована к большому бую за гаванью и навестить её можно только в полприлива; третий — что она сидит запертой в мейдстонской тюрьме за кражу детей; четвёртый — что её видели, как она села на метлу во время последнего сильного ветра и взяла курс прямо на Кале. Извозчики, которых я расспрашивал потом, были так же шутливы и так же непочтительны; а лавочники, которым не нравился мой вид, обычно отвечали, не выслушав, что мне нужно, что у них для меня ничего нет. Я чувствовал себя несчастнее и беднее, чем в любое другое время своего бегства. Деньги мои кончились, мне нечем было больше распорядиться; я был голоден, томим жаждой и измучен и казался таким же далёким от цели, как если бы остался в Лондоне.", "source_sha256": "e3938f73411f2229c85b4f81a3da3d71c61458944e0244779c26876f32b640fd", "target_id": "ru-en85-u015-b0062", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "0101f9bd4501f06553d93c604b0f9fc441a4b4cc5c18dd760982b1bf7d96b494"}, {"source_id": "en85-u015-b0063", "target": "Утро ушло на эти расспросы, и я сидел на пороге пустой лавки на углу улицы близ рыночной площади, раздумывая, не побрести ли мне к тем другим местам, которые были названы, когда мимо проезжал извозчик в своей коляске и уронил попону. Что-то добродушное в лице этого человека, когда я подал ему попону, придало мне смелости спросить, не знает ли он, где живёт мисс Тротвуд, хотя я задавал этот вопрос так часто, что он почти замирал у меня на устах.", "source_sha256": "8a2c4fc7a005c6ed274c268e731b500cc13ec4b7d7e64fd395d700ec9b84946d", "target_id": "ru-en85-u015-b0063", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "679623aa50e44da0fc454bb6280f0ef26d9e7c3ec6428f1d355b696a6864c9b5"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 13, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u015-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trotwood,’ said he. ‘Let me see. I know the name, too. Old lady?’", "sha256": "adc54e64077f850d908d0c15ab1edce08ae8088fe5e00b4d954b4a496d7dd455", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Yes,’ I said, ‘rather.’", "sha256": "8a784900f944d7d1c44398d0a86941975531cdbbaf5c6dea3fa1e86881b3e44a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Pretty stiff in the back?’ said he, making himself upright.", "sha256": "f7bd1bf1bb22197db9ffbcaa6ee0d1382a52ef661678944cc37bdb935716d3b4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Yes,’ I said. ‘I should think it very likely.’", "sha256": "15ee99b17839627a9868f5250538eddc239021db26397db597154a06de9b89d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Carries a bag?’ said he—‘bag with a good deal of room in it—is gruffish, and comes down upon you, sharp?’", "sha256": "067ea5965aca64302ca7acb4a369fa8687e0f7d1a90246a1b2969d0be52c06af", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My heart sank within me as I acknowledged the undoubted accuracy of this description.", "sha256": "9029264ba8f2fe11745741816e92eb5cd096f563f939635c63521cbd7dd901be", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why then, I tell you what,’ said he. ‘If you go up there,’ pointing with his whip towards the heights, ‘and keep right on till you come to some houses facing the sea, I think you’ll hear of her. My opinion is she won’t stand anything, so here’s a penny for you.’", "sha256": "db40e3b2631773feccb1508aeaa75e0a730d734d58801ce6c4f1e5186f3a366b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I accepted the gift thankfully, and bought a loaf with it. Dispatching this refreshment by the way, I went in the direction my friend had indicated, and walked on a good distance without coming to the houses he had mentioned. At length I saw some before me; and approaching them, went into a little shop (it was what we used to call a general shop, at home), and inquired if they could have the goodness to tell me where Miss Trotwood lived. I addressed myself to a man behind the counter, who was weighing some rice for a young woman; but the latter, taking the inquiry to herself, turned round quickly.", "sha256": "4881c9e18ac1a2b35bdf23b1cebf955fc6c0a740c656f5fd41ddcd3c2a04df54", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My mistress?’ she said. ‘What do you want with her, boy?’", "sha256": "3b1393553a4254d86e0f3f3bc5326855958e8842afe2f0dadd9b64928c7ba380", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I want,’ I replied, ‘to speak to her, if you please.’", "sha256": "9e28b1ba5b9b10382dc05035913a488981d1868f72a416db5ca7e55f9a7f79e6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To beg of her, you mean,’ retorted the damsel.", "sha256": "528df42ea0f9c91a67b813c0b380b48c91a492bdd826484cf169f1b189a9952e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ I said, ‘indeed.’ But suddenly remembering that in truth I came for no other purpose, I held my peace in confusion, and felt my face burn.", "sha256": "26bd4c6903b21e95d6c1ddca53c9195a1adcf6c580f28220bf6a5ab2a02c7bb5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt’s handmaid, as I supposed she was from what she had said, put her rice in a little basket and walked out of the shop; telling me that I could follow her, if I wanted to know where Miss Trotwood lived. I needed no second permission; though I was by this time in such a state of consternation and agitation, that my legs shook under me. I followed the young woman, and we soon came to a very neat little cottage with cheerful bow-windows: in front of it, a small square gravelled court or garden full of flowers, carefully tended, and smelling deliciously.", "sha256": "0e7fb79cf2fef6b2a8881cb24485f1448b8943b550a87d1d0ce329d89d3a2239", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘This is Miss Trotwood’s,’ said the young woman. ‘Now you know; and that’s all I have got to say.’ With which words she hurried into the house, as if to shake off the responsibility of my appearance; and left me standing at the garden-gate, looking disconsolately over the top of it towards the parlour window, where a muslin curtain partly undrawn in the middle, a large round green screen or fan fastened on to the windowsill, a small table, and a great chair, suggested to me that my aunt might be at that moment seated in awful state.", "sha256": "a00d2f38ed36209d1f1576a4af07716acb93e20fea4ea23abb31fea42a5fc1d4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My shoes were by this time in a woeful condition. The soles had shed themselves bit by bit, and the upper leathers had broken and burst until the very shape and form of shoes had departed from them. My hat (which had served me for a night-cap, too) was so crushed and bent, that no old battered handleless saucepan on a dunghill need have been ashamed to vie with it. My shirt and trousers, stained with heat, dew, grass, and the Kentish soil on which I had slept—and torn besides—might have frightened the birds from my aunt’s garden, as I stood at the gate. My hair had known no comb or brush since I left London. My face, neck, and hands, from unaccustomed exposure to the air and sun, were burnt to a berry-brown. From head to foot I was powdered almost as white with chalk and dust, as if I had come out of a lime-kiln. In this plight, and with a strong consciousness of it, I waited to introduce myself to, and make my first impression on, my formidable aunt.", "sha256": "cd3c2f84418856ac3cffe75312bbb986ecb51ea1195719a9ac96eb13ebd05f3b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The unbroken stillness of the parlour window leading me to infer, after a while, that she was not there, I lifted up my eyes to the window above it, where I saw a florid, pleasant-looking gentleman, with a grey head, who shut up one eye in a grotesque manner, nodded his head at me several times, shook it at me as often, laughed, and went away.", "sha256": "2ccf8d3c3a32fa9c63619638051594467787b413c83ecbaee502f60331c37253", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had been discomposed enough before; but I was so much the more discomposed by this unexpected behaviour, that I was on the point of slinking off, to think how I had best proceed, when there came out of the house a lady with her handkerchief tied over her cap, and a pair of gardening gloves on her hands, wearing a gardening pocket like a toll-man’s apron, and carrying a great knife. I knew her immediately to be Miss Betsey, for she came stalking out of the house exactly as my poor mother had so often described her stalking up our garden at Blunderstone Rookery.", "sha256": "161a98d92487aa7a9abc57ec7cfb961c034d24123eb79f29d7b068acb3bcd5b8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Go away!’ said Miss Betsey, shaking her head, and making a distant chop in the air with her knife. ‘Go along! No boys here!’", "sha256": "1db8b5784bcd64aa590823de503f732a7db2f2abf16a1c33c9880fdba7c56358", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I watched her, with my heart at my lips, as she marched to a corner of her garden, and stooped to dig up some little root there. Then, without a scrap of courage, but with a great deal of desperation, I went softly in and stood beside her, touching her with my finger.", "sha256": "2fdd19f1b84b9cc94dc6053178f7c9dad58121b2e9e32d94970b392c2c5f7d4f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If you please, ma’am,’ I began.", "sha256": "8c6fb11a2ff420f9c358cc87abf8fdb1696d440096f3fa735aa2d28cd45dcdaf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She started and looked up.", "sha256": "888ba4c9fdfbac5a93bfcf7e5f157a0a7b4c7b4b3c88c52536a91db38c061a3a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If you please, aunt.’", "sha256": "6637c3d1d7ea5d774221e94ec5d1d7680feb1ab40fdf36daf8f03cfe5fa30266", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘EH?’ exclaimed Miss Betsey, in a tone of amazement I have never heard approached.", "sha256": "ecdd655ac75291fb8d754d2541d90d3f7acadb1c40989eee4898eab13112f56d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If you please, aunt, I am your nephew.’", "sha256": "3768cdbfdf943eb759a8993b2bd8268aeff8cbb815579c1cca1c4e3977743fca", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, Lord!’ said my aunt. And sat flat down in the garden-path.", "sha256": "cf59008467f5bf0f9630b66aff4057bc6c01ed193f7e779fb9751a94705ce1fc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am David Copperfield, of Blunderstone, in Suffolk—where you came, on the night when I was born, and saw my dear mama. I have been very unhappy since she died. I have been slighted, and taught nothing, and thrown upon myself, and put to work not fit for me. It made me run away to you. I was robbed at first setting out, and have walked all the way, and have never slept in a bed since I began the journey.’ Here my self-support gave way all at once; and with a movement of my hands, intended to show her my ragged state, and call it to witness that I had suffered something, I broke into a passion of crying, which I suppose had been pent up within me all the week.", "sha256": "80db0a034dbc3acf0a7fdec55f052cb1a91c4562210f424ff9125b66ed98a3fc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt, with every sort of expression but wonder discharged from her countenance, sat on the gravel, staring at me, until I began to cry; when she got up in a great hurry, collared me, and took me into the parlour. Her first proceeding there was to unlock a tall press, bring out several bottles, and pour some of the contents of each into my mouth. I think they must have been taken out at random, for I am sure I tasted aniseed water, anchovy sauce, and salad dressing. When she had administered these restoratives, as I was still quite hysterical, and unable to control my sobs, she put me on the sofa, with a shawl under my head, and the handkerchief from her own head under my feet, lest I should sully the cover; and then, sitting herself down behind the green fan or screen I have already mentioned, so that I could not see her face, ejaculated at intervals, ‘Mercy on us!’ letting those exclamations off like minute guns.", "sha256": "bd1b6e51765e2cfb282f42eedd37188ff49fc4646a3e24f4b3f9d0313c2f5893", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "After a time she rang the bell. ‘Janet,’ said my aunt, when her servant came in. ‘Go upstairs, give my compliments to Mr. Dick, and say I wish to speak to him.’", "sha256": "e068c89d986ce930fdf3866d1b8ec7f617f014101767f8895d92b98a8aac9e03", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Janet looked a little surprised to see me lying stiffly on the sofa (I was afraid to move lest it should be displeasing to my aunt), but went on her errand. My aunt, with her hands behind her, walked up and down the room, until the gentleman who had squinted at me from the upper window came in laughing.", "sha256": "19ac62d3da42e33e27c1a3f99fd75ff65c62321a31d4c1e8deeeb4358d9ca578", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[20]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u015-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Dick,’ said my aunt, ‘don’t be a fool, because nobody can be more discreet than you can, when you choose. We all know that.
